title: Synthetic response factory + contract-assertion CLI for deterministic SDK streaming tests
creator: Ananya Patel
description: Problem: Our SDK streaming and retry behavior lacks a single, deterministic harness that teams can use to author fixtures, re-record failing traces, and assert contract-level equivalence against the Redwood API. Existing VCR and replay tooling capture responses, but they are brittle for streaming frames (partial tokens, control frames) and do not provide a repeatable developer experience for Python/TS/Go SDK teams.
background: We have recurring flakes in SDK CI when tests rely on live staging or ad-hoc recorded fixtures. Root causes include timing variance in streaming frames, missing event ordering assertions, and insufficient checks for backpressure/retry semantics. The goal is a synthetic response factory (SRF) that can emit deterministic sequences of frames (headers, tokens, delta patches, errors), plus a small CLI to run contract-assertions comparing live traces (or recorded VCR tapes) against a canonical contract. This will make streaming ergonomics tests portable across SDK languages and enable CI gating without heavy reliance on staging infra.
acceptance_criteria: Add a synthetic response factory library with language-agnostic JSON fixture spec that describes frame-level events (type, timestamp offset, payload, error) for streaming endpoints
Provide CLI `redwood-fixture assert` that compares a live trace or VCR recording to a fixture and produces a detailed diff (frame-level, token diffs, reorderings, and retry metadata)
Integrate fixture generator into Python/TS/Go SDK test harnesses and add 12 deterministic tests (4 per language) covering normal stream, mid-stream error+retry, backpressure, and partial-token frames
Add CI job `sdk/streaming-contracts` that fails on contract regressions and publishes a replay artifact on failure
Document re-record workflow and a hygiene rule: only update golden fixtures with a cross-language review and a linking PR referencing the change rationale
implementation_steps: Design fixture JSON schema and publish spec in Confluence (doc link in links)
Implement JavaScript prototype of SRF and CLI in /tools/stream-fixtures repo
Expose a minimal HTTP mockserver that can stream frames with configurable delays and injected transient errors
Add language bindings/wrappers: lightweight Python and Go helpers to consume fixture files and spin up local mockserver
Wire CLI to compute canonical diffs and return non-zero exit codes for CI failures
Create SDK test-suite changes and add gating job in CircleCI/GitHub Actions
Run cross-language fuzzer over fixture permutations to catch brittle comparisons
tradeoffs_and_risks: Fidelity vs speed: High-fidelity frames (byte-level fidelity, precise intervals) increase test runtime and flakiness; will support configurable fidelity levels
Maintenance burden: Golden fixtures can drift; enforce PR review + changelog to mitigate accidental rewrites
Security: Fixtures may contain masked tokens; ensure SRF strips live credentials and documents KMS usage for any stored traces
Scope creep: Avoid implementing a full fair-queueing mockserver — focus on deterministic control over frame ordering and delays
